dataSources: Cato tunnel / site connectivity events; `sourcetype=cato:events` or `cato:sase` Indexes: sase. Sourcetypes: cato:events, cato:sase. Key fields: site, tunnel_state. Validate field extraction in Search before saving the alert; compare event counts to the vendor admin console.
spl:
index=sase sourcetype IN ("cato:events","cato:sase") earliest=-7d
| eval site=coalesce(site_name, site_id, socket_name, socket_serial)
| eval tunnel_state=lower(coalesce(tunnel_state, tunnel_status, connection_state, link_state, ""))
| where match(tunnel_state,"down|disconnected|failed|lost|inactive|degraded") OR match(lower(coalesce(event_sub_type, "")),"(?i)tunnel.*down|socket.*down|disconnect")
| stats count earliest(_time) as first_event latest(_time) as last_event by site tunnel_state
| eval window_sec=last_event-first_event
| sort -count
description: Cato Sockets build IPsec/DTLS tunnels to the nearest PoP; when tunnels drop, the site loses cloud-delivered security, path selection, and centralized breakout. Measuring down events, duration, and time-to-recover supports SLA reporting and distinguishes transient blips from structural connectivity failures.
value: Network operations teams monitor Cato SD-WAN tunnel stability for every site — disconnection frequency, flapping detection, and PoP selection patterns — distinguishing between site-level ISP issues and Cato PoP-level problems for rapid root cause identification.
implementation: Align `event_sub_type` / `tunnel_state` values with Cato’s feed documentation (labels differ between API and syslog forwarding). For MTTR, run a companion search pairing down events with subsequent up events per `site_id`. Page on any site with sustained tunnel-down beyond your RTO threshold.
visualization: Single value (sites currently down), Timeline (tunnel state), Table (longest outages 7d), Line chart (daily down minutes per site).

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cato Networks SD-WAN tunnel events in `index=cato` with `sourcetype=cato:events` where `event_type=connectivity`. Key fields: `tunnel_state` (connected/disconnected), `tunnel_protocol` (DTLS/IPSec), `pop_name`, `site_name`, `socket_interface`, `uptime`, `reconnect_count`.
• Cato SD-WAN tunnels connect each site's Socket (edge device) to the nearest Cato PoP. Each socket maintains two tunnels (primary + secondary) for redundancy. Tunnel health is measured by: uptime, reconnect frequency, and PoP selection stability.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Verify tunnel events:
```spl
index=cato sourcetype="cato:events" event_type=connectivity earliest=-24h
| where isnotnull(tunnel_state)
| stats count by site_name, tunnel_state
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — Tunnel uptime and stability:
```spl
index=cato sourcetype="cato:events" event_type=connectivity tunnel_state=disconnected earliest=-7d
| stats count as disconnections dc(pop_name) as pops_affected by site_name, socket_interface
| sort - disconnections
```

Understanding this SPL: Counts tunnel disconnections per site/interface. A high disconnection count means the tunnel is unstable (flapping). If the same site disconnects from multiple PoPs, the issue is likely at the site (ISP, Socket hardware). If multiple sites disconnect from the same PoP, the issue is at the Cato PoP.

PoP selection analysis:
```spl
index=cato sourcetype="cato:events" event_type=connectivity tunnel_state=connected earliest=-7d
| stats count dc(pop_name) as pops_used values(pop_name) as pop_names by site_name
| where pops_used > 2
| sort - pops_used
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) In Cato Management: Topology > Sites > select site > Socket status.
(b) Reboot a Socket and verify the disconnect/reconnect sequence.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard: Row 1 — Tunnel status by site. Row 2 — Flapping sites. Row 3 — PoP diversity.
Alert: Immediate when a site has no active tunnels. Warning on >5 disconnections per day.

Runbook:
1. **Site with no tunnels** — Site offline. Check Socket power and ISP connectivity.
2. **Flapping tunnel** — ISP quality issue. Run diagnostics from Cato Management.
3. **Many PoPs** — Site may be bouncing between PoPs due to path instability.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **No tunnel events** — Socket may not be reporting. Check Socket connectivity.
• **All tunnels show 'connected'** — Events may only fire on state changes. Use Cato API for current state.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Cato Networks Events App (Splunkbase 8037); `eventsFeed.py` from [catonetworks/cato-splunk-integration](https://github.com/catonetworks/cato-splunk-integration)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cato:events, cato:sase into sase. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`site, tunnel_state`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Each office has a device that creates a secure tunnel to the cloud. We count how often each tunnel breaks and reconnects, because a tunnel that keeps dropping means the office is constantly losing its connection — like a phone call that keeps cutting out.
hardware: Cato Socket, Cato vSocket (site tunnel endpoints); Cato SDP Client uses separate session semantics — split dashboards accordingly.
